title: Rigveda 9.9: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.9: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.9 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 671r-671v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.9.1-4 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 32); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 671r
translation.original_text:
1pari̍ pri̱yā di̱vaḥ ka̱vir vayā̍ṁsi na̱ptyo̍r hi̱taḥ | su̱vā̱no yā̍ti ka̱vikra̍tuḥ ||
2pra-pra̱ kṣayā̍ya̱ panya̍se̱ janā̍ya̱ juṣṭo̍ a̱druhe̍ | vī̱ty a̍rṣa̱ cani̍ṣṭhayā ||
3sa sū̱nur mā̱tarā̱ śuci̍r jā̱to jā̱te a̍rocayat | ma̱hān ma̱hī ṛ̍tā̱vṛdhā̍ ||
4sa sa̱pta dhī̱tibhi̍r hi̱to na̱dyo̍ ajinvad a̱druha̍ḥ | yā eka̱m akṣi̍ vāvṛ̱dhuḥ ||
translation.text:
1THE Sage of Heaven whose heart is wise, when laid between both hands and pressed, Sends us delightful powers of life.
2On, onward to a glorious home; dear to the people void of guile, With excellent enjoyment, flow.
3He, the bright Son, when born illumed his Parents who had sprung to life, Great Son great Strengtheners of Law.
4Urged by the seven devotions he hath stirred the guileless rivers which Have magnified the Single Eye.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 671r (numbered 93r by the scribe) (OPenn image 671, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.8.4 ‹kṣipaḥ hinvanti sapta dhītayaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 671v (numbered 93v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.9.5 ‹mahe yuvānam ā dadhuḥ›. Verses 9.9.1-4 end on this page.

2pra-pra | kṣayāya | panyase | janāya | juṣṭaḥ | adruhe | vītī | arṣa | caniṣṭhayā
3saḥ | sūnuḥ | mātarā | śuciḥ | jātaḥ | jāte iti | arocayat | mahān | mahī | ṛta-vṛdhā
4saḥ | sapta | dhīti-bhiḥ | hitaḥ | nadyaḥ | ajinvat | adruhaḥ | yāḥ | ekam | akṣi | vavṛdhuḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 9.9.5-9 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 32); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 671v
translation.original_text:
5tā a̱bhi santa̱m astṛ̍tam ma̱he yuvā̍na̱m ā da̍dhuḥ | indu̍m indra̱ tava̍ vra̱te ||
6a̱bhi vahni̱r ama̍rtyaḥ sa̱pta pa̍śyati̱ vāva̍hiḥ | krivi̍r de̱vīr a̍tarpayat ||
7avā̱ kalpe̍ṣu naḥ puma̱s tamā̍ṁsi soma̱ yodhyā̍ | tāni̍ punāna jaṅghanaḥ ||
8nū navya̍se̱ navī̍yase sū̱ktāya̍ sādhayā pa̱thaḥ | pra̱tna̱vad ro̍cayā̱ ruca̍ḥ ||
9pava̍māna̱ mahi̱ śravo̱ gām aśva̍ṁ rāsi vī̱rava̍t | sanā̍ me̱dhāṁ sanā̱ sva̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
5These helped to might theYouthful One, high over all, invincible, Even Indu, Indra! in thy law.
6The immortal Courser, good to draw, looks down upon the Seven: the fount Hath satisfied the Goddesses
7Aid us in holy rites, O Man: O Pavamâna, drive away Dark shades that must be met in fight.
8Make the paths ready for a hymn newer and newer evermore: Make the lights shine as erst they shone.
9Give, Pavamâna, high renown, give kine and steeds and hero sons: Win for us wisdom, win the light.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 671v (numbered 93v by the scribe) (OPenn image 672, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.9.5 ‹mahe yuvānam ā dadhuḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 672r (numbered 94r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.10.6 ‹āyavaḥ›. Verses 9.9.5-9 end on this page; 9.9.5 begins on fol. 671r (numbered 93r by the scribe).
